chunks: 2326 - Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said in another report: a hadith in which Islam and faith are mentioned.
"And if a man were to enter the Ka'bah and urinate in it in defiance, he would be expelled from the Ka'bah and from the Haram, and his neck would be struck."

key_terms.الصَّادِقُ: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq عليه السلام, the transmitter of this teaching
key_terms.الْإِسْلَامُ: outward submission to the religion of Islam
key_terms.الْإِيمَانُ: faith, inward belief beyond mere outward Islam
key_terms.الْحَرَمِ: the sacred sanctuary surrounding the Ka'bah
key_terms.الْكَعْبَةَ: the Ka'bah, the sacred House in Makkah
key_terms.مُعَانِدًا: acting defiantly and in deliberate opposition

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on deliberately desecrating the Ka'bah in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith states a severe ruling for one who deliberately desecrates the sanctity of the Ka'bah out of defiance. It highlights the distinction between outward Islam and true iman by showing that intentional violation of the holiest sanctuary carries the gravest consequence.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2326 - Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) said in another narration, in a discussion about Islam and faith:
"If a man were to enter the Kaaba and urinate in it out of defiance, he would be removed from the Kaaba and the Haram, and his neck would be struck."
